situation (example wording): "How many juvenile robbery victims in Ohio in 2024?", "How many teen homicide victims in Chicago in 2024?", "child victims", "minor victims" (an age word beside a victim word)
what the app does today: Juvenile victims were declined and teen victims were read as under 18 (P30), while P107 made juvenile mean an offender under 18 and P105 read teenage as 13 to 19.
proposed behavior: When the question says victims, "juvenile", "minor", "child" and "kid" mean victims under 18, and "teen" and "teenage" mean victims aged 13 to 19, on every source and in every kind of question, with no ask. The answer states the age range used ("under 18", "aged 13 to 19"). "Teen" and "teenage" mean 13 to 19 on every side: offenders ("teen robbery offenders", "robberies by teens": "robbery offenses with an offender aged 13 to 19") and arrestees ("teen arrests for robbery": "robbery arrests of arrestees aged 13 to 19"). "Juvenile" with no victim word ("juvenile crime", "juvenile offenders", "juvenile arrests") stays P107: an offender or arrestee under 18. A bare "teen offenders" with no crime asks which kind of crime, like any offender question. The age word reads the same in the plural and after the crime ("teenagers arrested for robbery", "murders of teenagers", "children murdered", "with a teen victim"). A follow-up that names an age ("just the juveniles", "what about teen victims", "how many of the victims were children") puts it in the previous question; when the question names no person it asks "Do you mean teen victims, offenders or arrestees?", and when the follow-up names another person than the question counts it asks "Do you mean teen offenders instead of the victims counted?". A rate for an age group stays declined (no population base).
exact default or choices offered: Juvenile, minor, child, kid victims: under 18. Teen or teenage victims, offenders or arrestees: 13 to 19. Juvenile offenders or arrestees: under 18 (P107).
why: Jeff 2026-11-16: "Teen homicide victims is homicide victims 13-19, juvenile robbery victims are robbery victims defined as juvenile (under 18)." No buttons and no clarification: he found it obvious.
status: Decided (Jeff 2026-11-16); teen on every side (offenders and arrestees too) decided 2026-11-16 (through the coordinator)
